name: HouseCanary: AI Valuation and Forecasting for Real Estate
title: HouseCanary: AI Valuation and Forecasting for Real Estate
answer: HouseCanary is an AI-powered valuation and data platform covering more than 136 million U.S. properties, publishing research, product pages and case studies on its site. Its most useful single claim is a median absolute percentage error of 2.7% on post-list valuations and 7.5% pre-list, the accuracy figure institutional users would weigh when deciding whether to underwrite on automated valuations.

sections.body: HouseCanary publishes this material on housecanary.com, where the company presents itself as a 50-state brokerage and an AI-powered real estate data and analytics provider. The pages read include blog posts, research on 2026 forecasts, product descriptions, a case study and a technology page. The company says its solutions have used AI since inception, that its data is updated daily, and that it holds 35 years of historical data. It describes monthly internal testing and quarterly third-party testing of its products.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: HouseCanary's central product is an automated valuation model built with machine learning, alongside home price and rental price indices that forecast trends. The company says its models account for market volatility, local income and other price factors, and that its HPI allows comparison of submarkets within a metropolitan statistical area. Its Property Explorer produces client-ready reports with an estimate, valuation range, comparables and line-item adjustments, and CanaryAI answers plain-English questions with live market data. An MCP server connects assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to HouseCanary data through 149 endpoints. The company also describes propensity-to-list scoring, which ranks properties by their probability of listing in the next 90 days as percentiles against the whole market. Its research forecasts the steepest home price gains through 2026 in smaller markets rather than the largest or most expensive ones.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: HouseCanary reports a median absolute percentage error of 2.8% for its AVM in one post and 2.7% on listed homes with 7.5% pre-list in others, and says its valuation engine has generated over 122 million AVMs. It covers 136 million or more properties, and says 6 of the top 10 single family rental REIT operators and 8 of the top 10 private lenders use it. Its 2026 forecast puts Stevens Point and Plover, Wisconsin and Springfield, Ohio at +10.9%, Rochester, New York and Rockford, Illinois at 10.5%, and Erie, Pennsylvania at +10.1%. A case study reports four confirmed listings and two luxury listings worth $1.2 million and $1.5 million from a propensity model.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in the industry, this source shows how automated valuation is sold into institutional and lending workflows rather than to consumers. The error figures, the volume of AVMs generated and the named share of REIT operators and private lenders give a concrete sense of where machine learning valuation is already relied on. The propensity model case study shows a predictive score being used for listing acquisition, including the practical finding that the very highest scores were less actionable than the 87 to 95% band.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: The material is published by HouseCanary about its own products, so accuracy and adoption claims are self-reported and not independently verified on the pages read. Several posts are marketing-led, listing tools and benefits rather than presenting method or validation detail. The forecast covers only the next 12 months and a selected set of markets. The case study rests on one brokerage in two markets, so its conversion results are not generalisable.
